From the result you already have: sufficient_stats(t.test(extra ~ group, data = sleep), data = sleep) #> <reprokit sufficient_stats>  analysis: independent-samples t-test  (input: t.test) #> Verdict: apa_suffices #> Because: Summary statistics suffice: per-group n, mean and SD determine the reported results exactly. #> The numbers APA style asks a paper to report suffice to reproduce this analysis exactly. #> To publish: per-group n, mean and SD (appendix() writes this out). #> Disclosure check: passed (group sizes, threshold 5). #> Choices read from the t.test result: test = Welch. #> What readers lose compared with the raw data: #>   * checking the distribution and outliers within each group #>   * nonparametric or robust alternatives #> Statistics stored: n, mean, sd #> Sharing the raw data remains the standard (APA Publication Manual section 1.14, Ethics Code 8.14). sufficient_stats(chisq.test(table(mtcars$am, mtcars$vs))) #> <reprokit sufficient_stats>  analysis: chi-squared test of independence  (input: chisq.test) #> Verdict: apa_suffices #> Because: Summary statistics suffice: the contingency table of counts determine the reported results exactly. #> The numbers APA style asks a paper to report suffice to reproduce this analysis exactly. #> To publish: the contingency table of counts (appendix() writes this out). #> Disclosure check: passed (cell counts (a count above 0 and below 5 is flagged; zeros are not), threshold 5). #> Choices read from the chisq.test result: test = Yates. #> What readers lose compared with the raw data: #>   * checking that the expected counts are large enough for the chi-squared approximation (expected counts below 5; reprokit does not test this) #>   * exact, Fisher or Monte Carlo alternatives for sparse tables #>   * any variable other than the ones in the table #> Statistics stored: n #> Sharing the raw data remains the standard (APA Publication Manual section 1.14, Ethics Code 8.14).  # Mediation from two models, in either order: sufficient_stats(lm(hp ~ wt, data = mtcars), lm(mpg ~ wt + hp, data = mtcars)) #> <reprokit sufficient_stats>  analysis: simple mediation  (input: lm) #> Verdict: apa_plus_suffices #> Because: Summary statistics suffice: n, means and covariance matrix of X, M and Y determine the reported results exactly. #> The APA numbers alone do not reproduce this analysis exactly; these numbers beyond them are needed: #>   * the correlations is not implied by the APA numbers; reporting it makes the result exact (needed because the paths b and c′ depend on how X and M overlap, which the APA numbers do not show). #> To publish: n, means and covariance matrix of X, M and Y (appendix() writes this out). #> Disclosure check: passed (sample size only (no groups or cells; no individual values stored), threshold 5). #> What readers lose compared with the raw data: #>   * the bootstrap (or Monte Carlo) confidence interval of the indirect effect a*b #>   * residual diagnostics (normality, outliers, influence) #>   * refitting with covariates, other mediators or transformations #> Statistics stored: n, mean, cov #> Sharing the raw data remains the standard (APA Publication Manual section 1.14, Ethics Code 8.14).  # From numbers typed from a paper, no data needed: sufficient_stats(test = "paired", n = "30", m = c("5.1", "4.6"), sd = c("1.2", "1.3"),                  t = "2.1", df = "29") #> <reprokit sufficient_stats>  analysis: paired-samples t-test  (input: typed) #> Verdict: apa_plus_suffices #> Because: From the typed numbers: paired-samples t-test, the APA numbers need a further number to determine the result. #> The APA numbers alone do not reproduce this analysis exactly; these numbers beyond them are needed: #>   * r is implied between .10 and .70 by the APA numbers; reporting it makes the result exact (needed because the spread of the difference scores depends on how the two conditions correlate). #> Nothing is stored: typed numbers hold no reproducible summaries, so appendix() needs a model or data. #> What readers lose compared with the raw data: #>   * checking the distribution and outliers of the differences #>   * nonparametric or robust alternatives #> Sharing the raw data remains the standard (APA Publication Manual section 1.14, Ethics Code 8.14).  # A verdict, not an error, when summaries cannot do it: sufficient_stats(glm(am ~ wt, data = mtcars, family = binomial)) #> <reprokit sufficient_stats>  analysis: not recognised #> Verdict: needs_raw_data #> Because: reprokit does not cover glm/lm objects, so it cannot show that summary statistics are enough. #> Nothing is stored: summary statistics do not make this analysis reproducible. #> What readers lose without the raw data: #>   * exact reproduction of this analysis #> Instead you could: #>   * share the raw data (possibly under a data-use agreement) #>   * share synthetic data and report its utility (outside reprokit) #>   * offer federated analysis (e.g. DataSHIELD) #> Sharing the raw data remains the standard (APA Publication Manual section 1.14, Ethics Code 8.14).
